title: Compact git log graphs
description: The --oneline --graph --decorate trio turns git log into a readable branch map, and -20 caps it so huge histories stay fast. Invoke it as `git log --oneline --graph --decorate -20`; a concrete run looks like `git log --oneline --graph --decorate -20`. Runs on any system with git.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Extract any tarball
description: Swapping the z flag for J handles .tar.xz, and -C picks the destination so archives never spray the current directory. Invoke it as `tar -xzvf archive.tar.gz -C dest/`; a concrete run looks like `tar -xzvf release.tar.gz -C /opt/app`. Runs on Linux, macOS, WSL.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Mirror a directory with rsync
description: The trailing slash on the source decides whether the directory itself or only its contents are copied — the classic rsync gotcha. Invoke it as `rsync -avz --delete src/ dest/`; a concrete run looks like `rsync -avz --delete ./build/ user@host:/srv/app/`. Runs on Linux, macOS, WSL.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Find files by name fast
description: -name matches the basename with shell patterns; -iname makes it case-insensitive for sloppy filenames. Invoke it as `find <dir> -name "*.log" -mtime +7`; a concrete run looks like `find /var/log -name "*.log" -mtime +7`. Runs on Linux, macOS.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Recursive grep with context
description: -R walks directories, -n prints line numbers, and -C2 shows two lines of context so matches are actually understandable. Invoke it as `grep -Rn -C2 "TODO" src/`; a concrete run looks like `grep -Rn -C2 "TODO" src/`. Runs on Linux, macOS, WSL.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Sum a column with awk
description: awk splits each line on whitespace into $1, $2, ... so totalling a column is a one-liner with no Python needed. Invoke it as `awk '{s+=$2} END {print s}' file`; a concrete run looks like `awk '{s+=$3} END {print s}' sales.tsv`. Runs on Linux, macOS, WSL.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

t: In-place search and replace with sed
title: In-place search and replace with sed
description: The -i flag edits files in place; pairing it with a .bak extension keeps a backup until the expression is proven. Invoke it as `sed -i.bak "s/foo/bar/g" file`; a concrete run looks like `sed -i.bak "s/localhost/db.internal/g" app.conf`. Runs on Linux, macOS (BSD sed needs the extension argument).

fields.platform: Linux, macOS (BSD sed needs the extension argument)

provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Download with resume via curl
description: -C - resumes a broken download from where it stopped, and -L follows redirects that otherwise yield empty files. Invoke it as `curl -L -C - -o file url`; a concrete run looks like `curl -L -C - -o ubuntu.iso https://releases.ubuntu.com/22.04/ubuntu.iso`. Runs on Linux, macOS, Windows.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: SSH tunnel a local port
description: -L binds a local port to a remote service through the SSH server, exposing internal dashboards without opening firewall ports. Invoke it as `ssh -L 8080:localhost:80 user@host`; a concrete run looks like `ssh -L 8080:localhost:80 deploy@db01.internal`. Runs on any system with OpenSSH.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Run a throwaway container
description: --rm deletes the container on exit so experiments never accumulate; -it gives an interactive shell inside. Invoke it as `docker run --rm -it image <cmd>`; a concrete run looks like `docker run --rm -it python:3.12 python -c "print(42)"`. Runs on any system with Docker.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: List pods across namespaces
description: -A spans all namespaces at once, and -o wide adds the node and IP columns that plain output hides. Invoke it as `kubectl get pods -A -o wide`; a concrete run looks like `kubectl get pods -A -o wide`. Runs on any system with kubectl + cluster access.

fields.platform: any system with kubectl + cluster access

provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Slice JSON with jq
description: jq filters stream JSON without loading it into a script; .[] iterates arrays and select() filters objects. Invoke it as `jq '.[] | select(.ok)' data.json`; a concrete run looks like `jq '.items[] | select(.price < 10)' catalog.json`. Runs on Linux, macOS, Windows.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Convert video with ffmpeg
description: -crf 23 is the quality sweet spot for H.264 and -preset fast trades a little size for much faster encodes. Invoke it as `ffmpeg -i in.mov -c:v libx264 -crf 23 -preset fast out.mp4`; a concrete run looks like `ffmpeg -i talk.mov -c:v libx264 -crf 23 -preset fast talk.mp4`. Runs on Linux, macOS, Windows.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Detach-safe sessions with tmux
description: tmux keeps shells alive after the SSH connection drops; attach -t re-enters a named session by name. Invoke it as `tmux new -s work / tmux attach -t work`; a concrete run looks like `tmux new -s deploy`. Runs on Linux, macOS.

title: Check a service with systemctl
description: is-active answers in one word for scripts, while status shows the recent journal lines that explain failures. Invoke it as `systemctl is-active <svc> / systemctl status <svc>`; a concrete run looks like `systemctl status nginx`. Runs on Linux with systemd.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.
